_README: THREE SECTIONS WITH THREE DIFFERENT JOBS. They are reported separately and never summed,
because summing them produces a number that answers no question anybody has.
works    - phrased the way a person actually asks, months later. THIS is 'does it work'.
Expected: nearly all at rank 1. If this section drops, there is a bug.
boundary - the documented edge: questions sharing ZERO content words with their answer.
Expected NOT to return the file. These are not failures and are not scored as
such -- they are what the limit looks like, shown deliberately so a user meets it
here rather than by surprise in their own corpus.
absent   - topics genuinely not in the corpus. Must return nothing. Proves the matcher does
not fabricate. Cannot fail for a broken system, so it is never scored either.
WHY THIS SPLIT EXISTS (the correction that produced it): the boundary probes used to sit in
the same table as the real ones, turning a documented limit into a headline 'MISS' and a score
that looked like mediocrity. It measured how adversarially the probes were written, not how
well retrieval works. Asking a strategy note whether the sky is blue is not a hard query, it is
a nonsense one, and scoring it manufactures a failure that never happened.
NOTE the-cache-key-omitted-the-locale appears in BOTH works and boundary, on purpose. Same
file, same system, two phrasings -- one lands at rank 1 and one returns nothing. That pair is
the clearest single demonstration of what actually governs this tool.

boundary.why: country/region, money/currency, people/users -- synonym bridges. Shares no content word with the file, or with any other file in the corpus. Compare the 'works' entry for the same file: one word of shared vocabulary is the entire difference.
